agent.name: Promethean Technology Classification Agent
agent.specialty: Technology significance and bounded application implications

analytical_question: Should this hypothetical hotel launch multi-floor supply delivery, and does the significance of indoor autonomous delivery robots justify bypassing integration checks?
general_et_finding: Prospective classification: Breakthrough, with moderate confidence, for the complete indoor wheeled autonomous-delivery system relative to staff carrying or pushing a cart. E2 describes bounded restaurant transport capability and E3 reports a building-integration test. The candidate barrier is the need for a person to accompany each conventional carrying trip. That is a workflow constraint, not a universal historical condition: automated transport already existed, and the physical journey remains necessary. E4 documents continued operating and human-support requirements. Removing this robot class would plausibly bring back manual trips and carts rather than collapse multiple established societal systems; that is inference, not a tested shutdown. A hotel and a restaurant are both economic settings, not two independently dissolved tiers. No credible cross-tier categorical dissolution is established, so Potential Promethean is not justified under E1. Six-criterion scoring is NOT REACHED after the failed gate. Missing evidence concerns a defined 10x improvement, widespread cross-tier dissolution, a civilizational paradigm shift, dependent secondary innovation, democratized access and irreversible dependence. Autonomous execution of a bounded route is a meaningful capability change; elevator integration adds requirements without changing the general evidence or classification.
application_finding: Routine supply delivery could extend the hotel's service workflow, but the end-to-end application includes loading, access, elevator dispatch, handoff and recovery. Staff remain responsible for guest service. A reported elevator-capable configuration does not make every indoor delivery robot a multi-floor system.
organization_specific_finding: The aggressive/leading-edge hotel has staff support but has not verified elevator, door, connectivity or secure-handoff integration. E3 demonstrates a reported test in another setting, not compatibility here. Its posture can justify an early feasibility assessment, but cannot convert unresolved integration into launch readiness.
contrary_evidence_or_limitations: E3 is a historical supplier report, not a universal compatibility test or local acceptance result.
Model-specific manuals and generic navigation documentation cannot certify the proposed hotel configuration.
No local integration, guest-accessibility, time-saving or service-cost outcome is available.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in a bounded Breakthrough classification relative to manual carrying. Low confidence in immediate end-to-end hotel readiness because site interfaces are unverified. These are hypothetical organizational conditions and a significance interpretation; no safe-deployment certification is made.
value_opportunity_implication: The potential is fewer routine staff trips while maintaining guest access. Integration, failed handoffs and staff recovery could offset that benefit; evaluate total human effort rather than trips avoided alone.
risk_governance_implication: Facilities and front-desk managers should own integration acceptance, pedestrian access, guest handoff and manual recovery. Use a model designed for the proposed task; do not inherit elevator capability from a tray-robot description. Avoid unnecessary guest identifiers in test logs.
recommendation_management_implication: Do not begin unattended multi-floor guest-floor service now. Conduct a six-week staged feasibility and integration assessment with the robot and elevator providers and hotel facilities team. Start with supervised dry runs using non-sensitive supplies; proceed to a limited service pilot only after documented elevator, door, route and recovery acceptance. Proposed baseline: the same staff-delivered supply routes. Log total staff minutes including loading, handoff and rescue; end-to-end completion time; failed or wrong-destination deliveries; interventions; and elevator or access conflicts. The facilities manager owns integration checks and the front-desk manager owns service logging. Proposed expansion gate: verified interfaces, positive net staff-time savings and service reliability no worse than the manual baseline, with no unresolved access or safety problem. Stop on a door/elevator access failure that cannot be safely recovered, wrong-recipient release, blocked essential access or a hazardous incident; use staff delivery. These are proposed management controls, not measured results or certified thresholds.
change_monitoring_triggers: Reassess the local decision when interface tests, guest handoff, staff effort, failure counts, service time or costs become known.
Reassess broad significance only on credible multi-tier categorical dissolution and durable dependency, rather than additional vendor integrations alone.
Review significance annually over three years; refresh compatibility evidence before procurement.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Require actual elevator-provider approval, robot-model compatibility and recovery testing before live multi-floor use.
Withhold a safety guarantee, quantified ROI and staff-replacement conclusion.
Do not classify the technology as Potential or Confirmed Promethean on these sources.

evidence.claim: E1: Chapter 11 distinguishes constraint reduction from categorical dissolution and requires the system, suppression and tier tests.
evidence.source_or_reference: Fortino, Chapter 11, Identifying Promethean Technologies, August 2026 draft Rev 0.1, sections 11.2 and 11.7, pp. 3-4 and 8-11; supplied course PDF.
evidence.notes: Conceptual lens, not empirical performance evidence.

evidence.claim: E2: PUDU describes BellaBot Pro delivery modes, obstacle sensing and a 65 cm path-clearance specification.
evidence.notes: Supplier claim, not independent safety or ROI evidence. The page labels dish recognition and broadcast as under development; do not treat that feature as deployed.

evidence.claim: E3: PUDU reports a FlashBot elevator-integration test with Nippon Otis.
evidence.notes: Historical supplier report, not proof of compatibility with an arbitrary hotel elevator or independent long-run service performance.

evidence.claim: E4: The Servi Plus manual requires operating-space checks, mapping, human handoff and monitoring during peak periods.
evidence.notes: Read safety and use sections, printed pp. 6, 10, 16 and 19. Model-specific limits do not transfer automatically to PUDU products; supports a bounded example of continuing human responsibilities.

evidence.claim: E5: Nav2 documentation explains how robot footprint and local navigation configuration affect passage through space.
evidence.notes: General technical illustration, not proof that either named robot uses Nav2 or is safe in a specific venue.
